clue.text: Grotesque U-turn Alan gets fired!

indicators.note: something fired is set off and sent flying, so the letters of the two words are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone called Alan has been sacked for a policy reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets fired' rearranges the letters UTURN and ALAN together. The surface is about a man losing his job over a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grotesque is bizarrely distorted, far from what is normal or found in nature.

clue.text: Do not begin to shake lower part

indicators.note: telling the word not to begin means its opening letters are dropped

parts.note: to shake is to shudder

explanation.surface: An instruction not to start trembling, followed by a vague mention of a part lower down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do not begin to' cuts the opening SH from SHUDDER. The joke is in 'lower': not 'more low' but 'one that lows', a cow, whose udder is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow is a lower because it moos; the milk-giving bag beneath it is one of its parts.

clue.text: Pressed by demand, small-time lout primarily going inside …

indicators.note: the picked letters go into the middle of the word for demand, which holds them

parts.note: to demand something is to need it

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letters of small, time and lout

explanation.surface: Someone harassed by a small-time thug's demands, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small-time' counts as two words here, so 'primarily' gets two letters from it. The ellipsis joins the surface to the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestled can mean pressed snugly against something, as a child cuddled close to a parent.

clue.text: … caught on the run, whacked by this

definitions.text: … caught on the run, whacked by this

indicators.note: something whacked is knocked about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the lout, caught while fleeing, is beaten with a police weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whacked' rearranges C plus ONTHERUN. The whole clue also describes what a policeman's baton does to a fleeing lout, so it is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A British policeman's baton was what fleeing villains got clubbed with.

clue.text: Drink with chat over that's a blow

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the word for chat on top of the drink

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chattering on
punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl

explanation.surface: Having a drink and a chat seems a gentle pastime that ends in someone being struck.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit (on)' is British informal for talking at length. A rabbit punch is a chop to the back of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit punch is a short sharp chop to the back of the neck, a kind of strike.

clue.text: Get over opponent in court

parts.note: reads like beating a rival in a lawsuit, but the court is a tennis court and the shot goes over the opposing player's head

explanation.surface: Advice on beating your adversary in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a high looping shot sends the ball over the head of a player at the net.

clue.text: Prophet points after a short while

indicators.note: after places the points behind the short while

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short while
S, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A religious seer whose words come shortly afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is short for 'moment'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew prophet led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the commandments.

clue.text: To be one she must have been one

definitions.text: To be one she must have been one

parts.words: To be one she must have been one
parts.note: a riddle: to become a mother a woman must first have been someone's partner, and the Latin word for mother also hides that partner word

explanation.surface: A riddle about a woman who can only become something by having been something first.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an agent noun, 'one who mates': to become a mother (Latin mater, old British public-school slang for mum) a woman must first have mated.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, used jokingly in Britain for one's mum.

clue.text: Mirrors found in damaged capsule

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of capsule are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Reflective glass discovered inside a broken pill casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges CAPSULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Specula is the plural of speculum, a mirror, especially one in a telescope or a medical instrument.

clue.text: Left going in several directions without any reason

indicators.note: going in puts the letter for left inside the string of directions

parts.note: S, E, N, S, E, E, S and S are compass directions

explanation.surface: Someone who departed, scattering every which way for no reason at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points run S-E-N-S-E-E-S-S, and L goes in after the fifth.
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless acts are pointless, lacking any rational motive.

clue.text: Stir up very dry chap in retreat

indicators.note: retreat means going backwards, so the two words are read from the end

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
Sid is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: Agitating a very dull man who has withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns BRUTSID into DISTURB. 'very dry' looks like it means dull but is the wine term.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to agitate or unsettle something.

clue.text: Trace one bird and another

parts.note: a trace is a tiny bit
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Tracking one bird and then a second.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word: 'another' bird, after 'one bird' supplies TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like marsh bird, so it is a second bird alongside the first.

clue.text: Souvenir left in German state, almost

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the shortened state
almost means the last letter of the German state is lost

parts.note: the Reich was the German empire or state

explanation.surface: A keepsake left behind in a part of Germany, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts REICH to REIC, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something kept as a reminder of the past, a keepsake.

clue.text: Insist merino tup should be shot

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or spoilt, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone demanding that a merino ram be put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges MERINOTUP. A tup is a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to press someone persistently with requests, to keep on at them.

clue.text: Reap glamour in a baroque manner, such as the Victorians loved?

indicators.note: baroque style is ornate and twisted, so the letters are elaborately rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to gather glamour in an ornate style, of a kind admired in the nineteenth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a baroque manner' rearranges REAPGLAMOUR. Charades and similar indoor games were a Victorian family pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoor games such as charades played by families in the front room were a favourite Victorian evening entertainment.

clue.text: Ultimately drawn to Cupid's bow

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone finally attracted to the archery weapon of the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes N, O and D. 'bow' is not the archer's weapon but a bow of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow of the head is a small dip, a gesture of greeting or assent.

clue.text: Express, say, all points in theory only?

parts.note: N, E, W and S are all four compass points
something on paper exists only in theory

explanation.surface: A query about stating every argument as purely theoretical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express is a British daily paper, so 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express is a British daily, one example of the press.

clue.text: Poor "King" ape meets its end falling off here

definitions.text: Poor "King" ape meets its end falling off here

indicators.note: poor means in a bad state, so the gathered letters are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the final letter of the word its drops away, leaving only its first two letters

explanation.surface: Pity King Kong, the giant film ape, who dies falling from this New York skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end falling off' cuts ITS to IT, and 'Poor' rearranges R, APE, MEETS and IT. Read whole, the clue also describes King Kong's death fall from the skyscraper.
explanation.definitionFit: In the 1933 film, King Kong climbs the New York skyscraper and falls from the top to his death.

clue.text: Female's record written with fine antique pen

parts.note: she is a female; the 's links the pieces
an EP is an extended-play record
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
antique means old

explanation.surface: A woman's writing done with a delicate old pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is not a writing pen but an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is an enclosure for livestock, and this one holds sheep.

clue.text: Organised ladies holding sign — "Novel novel

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Organised ladies holding sign — "Novel novel (5,2,4)'. The fifteensquared blog reads it as W(OMEN)I + (novel)* = 'novel novel', plus a third 'novel' as the definition, but the held text has only two, so a word is missing and no scan is available.

clue.text: Amid secrets, bomb set up for gangster

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the hidden letters read upwards
amid means the letters are found within the words secrets and bomb

explanation.surface: A terrorist plants an explosive among classified material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amid' finds RETSBOM inside 'secrets, bomb'; 'set up' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster is a member of a criminal gang.

clue.text: For starters, women aren't short-lived

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A claim that, initially at least, women do not die young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short-lived' splits: 'short' gives its first letter and 'lived' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived is to have existed, the past tense of being.

clue.text: He painted engineer by water for Monet

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine
eau is French for water, the word the French painter would use

explanation.surface: An artist who painted an engineer next to the water instead of Monet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Monet' means 'in French', since Monet was French.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was the French Rococo painter of fêtes galantes.

clue.text: One possibly damned needs capsule of butanol, one carried by drug dealer

indicators.note: carried by means the dealer holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a pusher sells illegal drugs

indicators.note: a capsule is an outer shell, so the first and last letters of butanol

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doomed person needs a chemical in a capsule, supplied by a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsule of' takes B and L from butanol. 'Publish and be damned' was the Duke of Wellington's reply to a blackmailer.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'publish and be damned' implies whoever prints the story may be damned for it.

clue.text: Long after thought that's perfect

indicators.note: after places the letter for long behind the thought

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A long time after thinking, something proves flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, matching the best imaginable standard.

clue.text: Bread, at the end, is round

indicators.note: round means turning the two pieces about so they read backwards

parts.note: a tip is an end, as of a finger

explanation.surface: A remark that bread finished off is circular in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns ATTIP into PITTA. 'round' looks like a description of the flat bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern loaf that opens into a pocket.

clue.text: He told stories of rising main needing work

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for main is read upwards

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A storyteller speaking of a water main that needs repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SEA into AES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables.

clue.text: Animal found in paraguay and china?

indicators.note: found in places the animal inside the letters for the country

parts.note: PY is the international vehicle registration for Paraguay
an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature discovered in two countries, one in South America and one in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is not the country but porcelain, an example of ceramic ware, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, one kind of ceramic ware.

clue.text: Poet having refusal suppressed, OK?

indicators.note: suppressed means the refusal is held down and removed from the poet's name

parts.note: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a poet who has had a rejection silenced is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes is not a household name; taking NO from NOYES leaves the affirmative.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Yes?' asks for agreement, just as 'OK?' does.

clue.text: Caves to bats or birds

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Caverns given over to flying mammals or to feathered creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals of the caves but means mad, rearranging CAVESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocets are wading birds with upturned bills.

clue.text: Pastoral feature of Kazakhstan, literally?

definitions.meaning: the River Ural flows through Kazakhstan; written as R for river plus URAL it spells the word

explanation.surface: A rustic aspect of a Central Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' asks you to read the letters: R, the abbreviation for river, then URAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural and pastoral both describe the countryside and farming life.

clue.text: Jaguars may hasten after me

parts.note: reads as big cats chasing someone, but Jaguars are cars that slow for a road hump and then accelerate past it

explanation.surface: A person being chased by big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ridge across a road forces drivers to slow down, after which they speed up again.
